title: Podocyte Counting and Density Analysis Protocol
author: Jeff Hodgin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.565g9g6
materials: Use Pap Pen to encircle tissue
Stop reaction in dH ² O
Counterstain with Tacha’s Hematoxylin for 3 minutes

steps.title: Prepare and Deparaffinize Slides
steps.instruction: Prepare slides for staining by baking and removing paraffin.

substeps.instruction: Bake slides for 10 minutes at 60ºC (if not previously baked)
Wash 2x in xylene for 5 minutes
Wash 2x in 100% EtOH for 3 minutes
Wash 1x in 95% EtOH for 3 minutes
Wash 1x in 70% EtOH for 3 minutes
Rinse with dH2O

steps.title: Perform Antigen Retrieval
steps.instruction: Retrieve antigens using a PT Link system.

substeps.instruction: Place slides in PT Link containing 1x antigen retrieval reagent (pH 9)
Incubate at 97ºC for 20 minutes
Allow machine temperature to cool to 70ºC

steps.title: Block Endogenous Peroxidase and Background
steps.instruction: Block the tissue to reduce non-specific staining.

substeps.instruction: Wash in TBST for 5 minutes
Encircle tissue using Pap Pen
Block with Peroxidase 1 for 5 minutes
Wash 2x in 1x TBST for 2 minutes
Block with Background Sniper for 5 minutes
Wash 2x in TBST for 2 minutes

steps.title: Apply WT-1 Primary Antibody
steps.instruction: Incubate slides with the primary antibody.

substeps.instruction: Dilute WT-1 antibody in Da Vinci Green diluent at a 1:200 ratio
Incubate for 2 hours at room temperature in a humidified chamber
Wash 2x in TBST for 2 minutes

steps.title: Apply Secondary Detection Reagents
steps.instruction: Apply the probe and HRP polymer for signal amplification.

substeps.instruction: Incubate with Mach 3 Rabbit Probe for 20 minutes
Wash 2x in TBST for 2 minutes
Incubate with Mach 3 Rabbit HRP Polymer for 20 minutes
Wash 2x in TBST for 3 minutes

steps.title: Develop and Counterstain
steps.instruction: Visualize the staining and apply a nuclear counterstain.

substeps.instruction: Develop with Betazoid DAB-CHROMOGENK for 5 minutes; check staining intensity under a microscope
Stop the reaction in dH2O
Counterstain with Tacha’s Hematoxylin for 3 minutes
Rinse in dH2O to check intensity (reapply hematoxylin if necessary)
Rinse in TBST until blue
Wash with dH2O

steps.title: Dehydrate and Mount Slides
steps.instruction: Dehydrate the tissue and seal with a cover glass.

substeps.instruction: Wash in 70% EtOH for 2 minutes
Wash in 95% EtOH for 2 minutes
Wash 2x in 100% EtOH for 2 minutes
Wash in xylene for 8 minutes
Mount slides with 1 drop of mounting medium
Carefully insert cover glass, avoiding bubbles

steps.title: Capture Glomerular Images
steps.instruction: Calibrate the microscope and camera, then photograph the tissue.

substeps.instruction: Calibrate camera and microscope and load values into MetaMorph® Program
Photograph 50 consecutive glomerular cross-sections, moving systematically from outer cortex to inner cortex and back
Use phase contrast to ensure podocyte nuclei appear golden

steps.title: Measure Glomerular Area
steps.instruction: Use MetaMorph Image Analysis Software (version 6.1) to determine the area of the glomerular tuft.

substeps.instruction: Open images in MetaMorph
Select 'Measure' > 'Calibrate Distance', highlight 40x calibration, and click 'Apply'
Use the 'Polygon' tool to outline the glomerular tuft area
Select 'Measure' > 'Region Measurement' to obtain the area

steps.title: Count Podocyte Nuclei
steps.instruction: Count WT-1 positive nuclei using a size-restriction method to avoid counting granules.

substeps.instruction: Select 'Measure' > 'Manually Count Objects' and select the number 6
Count the nucleus only if the size restriction (number 6) fits within the nuclear profile; do not count if it is larger than the WT-1 positive area

steps.title: Analyze Podocyte Density and Volume
steps.instruction: Perform calculations based on 100 consecutive cross sections per animal (50 thick at 9 microns, 50 thin at 3 microns).

substeps.instruction: Calculate average podocyte number (P) and average glomerular area (GA) for each set of 50 sections
Calculate podocyte number per glomerular area (P/GA = P / GA) for both 3 and 9 micron sections
Determine P/GA Δ (the difference between P/GA of thick and thin sections)
Calculate average glomerular volume per podocyte (GV/P = 6.3 / P/GA Δ)
Calculate glomerular radius (R = (GA/π)^1/2) for both thicknesses
Calculate average radius (Rav) and average maximum radius (Rmax = 4Rav / π)
Calculate average glomerular volume (GV = 4/3π(Rmax)^3)
Calculate total podocyte number per glomerulus (P = GV / (GV/P))
